identity.name: Octyl gallate
identity.chemical_class: Alkyl gallate (gallic acid ester), phenolic antioxidant

function.mechanism: Phenolic chain-breaking antioxidant that inhibits lipid oxidation; classified in JECFA as a food additive antioxidant.
common_food_categories: Food supplements in solid form (EU retained category 17.1)
Margarine or oleomargarine (US standard-of-identity preservative context)

adi.basis: EFSA 2015 re-evaluation reported inability to establish an ADI for broader uses; no safety concern for then-current solid food supplement use at maximum permitted level, as cited in Regulation (EU) 2018/1462.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA could not establish a general ADI and EU subsequently removed uses except food supplements category 17.1.

adi.basis: JECFA octyl gallate entry lists NO ADI ALLOCATED (evaluation year 1996; temporary ADI from 1993 not extended).

concerns.summary: A 2023 in vitro human lymphocyte study reported no major genotoxic effect across several endpoints, but did find increased sister chromatid exchange and reduced mitotic index at higher tested concentrations.
A 2024 mouse study reported altered fecal microbiome diversity/community structure after octyl gallate administration.
EU risk management narrowed authorized uses after EFSA reported insufficient data to establish a broad ADI.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA-derived conclusion cited by EU legal text: no safety concern for retained solid food supplement use at maximum level.
IARC classification dataset search found no octyl gallate listing.
2023 in vitro study did not show major genotoxic action at tested concentrations despite some high-dose cellular effects.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric EFSA or JECFA ADI is currently available for straightforward exceedance comparison; risk control is mainly through use restriction.

risk_assessment.rationale: Octyl gallate remains allowed in some jurisdictions but with significant caveats: EFSA could not establish a broad ADI and EU removed most uses, while recent mechanistic/in vitro signals are not strong enough to indicate high risk at current regulated uses.
key_factors: EFSA ADI not established for broader uses
EU legal restriction to food supplements category 17.1
US use-specific approval in margarine standard
